# Invariant coverage

This map identifies checked-in regressions and the claims they support. It does not establish deployed bytecode equivalence, complete stateful coverage or a successful live payment. Test names link to their source files; execution results belong to the relevant CI run or release acceptance record.

| Invariant | Supporting regressions |
| --- | --- |
| Settlement conserves payer funds across provider and vault shares, including 0% and 100% provider rates; a failed payout rolls back the transaction. | [AtomicSettlement.t.sol](../../_backend/contracts/test/AtomicSettlement.t.sol): `testZeroAndFullProviderRatesConservePayment`, `testModelPaymentPaysRegisteredProviderAndRecordsActualVolume`, `testSecondLegFailureRollsBackProviderTransferAndMandate`. |
| A payment or signed authorization cannot charge twice or change payer, amount, route or mandate binding. | [AtomicSettlement.t.sol](../../_backend/contracts/test/AtomicSettlement.t.sol): `testPaymentReplayCannotDoubleSpendMandate`, `testAuthorizedPaymentRejectsRelayerRoutingSubstitution`, `testSignedPaymentReplayAndMalformedSignatureRejected`. [PaymentsAndMandates.t.sol](../../_backend/contracts/test/PaymentsAndMandates.t.sol): `testSettlementReplayCannotChargeTwice`, `testStrangerCannotDrainApprovedPayerAllowance`. |
| FeeVault distributes every unreserved unit, including rounding dust; reserved buyback funds are not redistributed. | [PaymentsAndMandates.t.sol](../../_backend/contracts/test/PaymentsAndMandates.t.sol): `testFuzzVaultSplitDistributesEntireBalanceIncludingDust`. [RewardsAndBuybacks.t.sol](../../_backend/contracts/test/RewardsAndBuybacks.t.sol): `testBuybackReserveIsOnlyTenPercentOfTreasuryAndNeverRedistributed`, `testBuybackCannotConsumeUndistributedFeesBeyondReserve`. |
| Stake ownership and accounting are preserved; rewards follow measured deposits and cannot be claimed twice or captured by a late depositor. | [TokenAndStaking.t.sol](../../_backend/contracts/test/TokenAndStaking.t.sol): `testFuzzStakeAndPartialUnstakePreserveAccounting`, `testStakersCannotWithdrawEachOthersFunds`. [RewardsAndBuybacks.t.sol](../../_backend/contracts/test/RewardsAndBuybacks.t.sol): `testRewardsAreProportionalToActualStakeAndClaimedOnce`, `testLateStakeCannotStealAlreadyReceivedFees`, `testFuzzRewardClaimsNeverExceedMeasuredDeposits`. |
| Callback-enabled listing tokens cannot create duplicate model/code listings through either registry entrypoint; the guard resets after success or rollback. | [RegistryReentrancy.t.sol](../../_backend/contracts/test/RegistryReentrancy.t.sol): `testListBlocksNestedListDuplicate`, `testListBlocksNestedPolicyListDuplicate`, `testPolicyListBlocksNestedListDuplicate`, `testPolicyListBlocksNestedPolicyListDuplicate`, `testListingGuardResetsAfterSuccess`, `testRejectedStakeRollsBackAndResetsListingGuard`. |
| Mixed listing, time advance, approval, permanent production-chain revocation and unauthorized governance preserve model/policy identity, stake, refunds and allowances; current/cached v1/v2 receipts obey the selected signer and EIP-712 domain. | [GovernanceStatefulInvariant.t.sol](../../_backend/contracts/test/GovernanceStatefulInvariant.t.sol): `invariant_RegistryStakePolicyAndPermanentRevocation`, `invariant_SignerGovernanceAndReceiptAdmission`, `test_SeededMixedLifecycleHasPositiveAndNegativeCoverage`. Independent ghost accounting and manual EIP-712 digests are checked after mixed actions. A separate named profile explores 128 histories of depth 128 with 13 explicit handler selectors; the deterministic test asserts reachable successful and rejected branches. |
| Durable transaction coordination allocates unique nonces, reuses identical signed bytes for one operation and reconciles chain success without a second charge. | [durable.integration.test.ts](../../_backend/apps/api/src/durable.integration.test.ts): “allocates distinct nonces across four independent OS processes”, “concurrent processes retry one operation with the identical transaction”, “rejects operation-key reuse for a different transfer”, “recovers a crash with signed bytes saved (broadcast had happened: %s)”, “reconciles chain success followed by database finalization failure without charging twice”. These cases require isolated PostgreSQL and Anvil integration infrastructure. |
| Wallet challenges are single-use, client quotas do not let one caller exhaust another caller's allowance, and Redis quotas remain atomic and TTL-bounded. | [wallet-auth.test.ts](../../_backend/apps/api/src/wallet-auth.test.ts): “allows only one concurrent use of a signed challenge”, “exhausting one client cannot block another client's challenge, verify, resume or logout”. [wallet-auth.integration.test.ts](../../_backend/apps/api/src/wallet-auth.integration.test.ts): “enforces five pending challenges per client/address across racing store instances”, “admits exactly five racing requests across clients, preserving independent quotas and the original TTL”, “expires quota counters and restores a bounded TTL for a preexisting counter with no expiry”. The integration cases require isolated PostgreSQL or a real Redis service; mocked unit results do not substitute for Redis execution. |

The Foundry suite includes fuzz regressions, deterministic adversarial cases and a bounded stateful governance campaign. These are not exhaustive sequence proofs. The campaign covers registry/receipt governance, not payment settlement; ordinary refund accounting is checked, but the malicious-token fixture hooks listing `transferFrom`, not refund `transfer` callbacks. Economic entrypoint guards in UsageMeter and InsuranceStaking also have source review; their existing accounting tests must not be described as dedicated malicious-token callback coverage.

Routine tests and coverage use 32 histories of depth 64. The main workflow also runs the longer profile with a fixed reproducible seed. From `_backend` on Linux with pinned Forge installed:

```sh
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=stateful npm run test:contracts -- --match-contract GovernanceStatefulInvariantTest --fuzz-seed 0x20261007
```

The two invariant assertions share one campaign, so 128 × 128 means 16,384 combined handler calls, not twice that count. Execution counts and source hashes belong to the relevant recorded run; they are not a deployed governance readback.

Local tests, scanner results and CI jobs use development fixtures and isolated infrastructure. Live wallet recovery, deployed contract correspondence, real USDC settlement, provider evidence and Arc receipt acceptance remain separate checks. No scanner result establishes those guarantees by itself. See [scanner policy](README.md) and [release acceptance](../../docs/e1-release.md).
